newsitem.title: GERMANY: Peter Graf to finish tax-evasion sentence in jail.
newsitem.headline: Peter Graf to finish tax-evasion sentence in jail.

text.p: Peter Graf, the disgraced father of tennis star Steffi Graf, will move from a prison hospital to a regular jail to serve the rest of his sentence for tax evasion, justice authorities said on Monday.
Convicted of evading millions of dollars' worth of tax on his daughter's income, Graf was sentenced in January to three years and nine months in jail.
He will probably only have to serve two thirds of his sentence in total, meaning he may be out of prison as early as next year because he has already served 15 months in investigative custody.

Justice officials in Baden-Wuerttemberg state said Graf, convicted of evading or trying to evade 12 million marks ($6.5 million) in taxes, began his jail term in a prison hospital in Hohenaspert last month because he wanted a health check-up.
It was unclear when he would be transferred to the jail in Ulm, which is about 160 km (100 miles) west of Munich.

The Mannheim court that released Graf on bail last November ordered him to undergo psychotherapy. His mental health during his time in investigative custody was the subject of German newspaper speculation.
Steffi's father has been the most important figure in the life of the former world number one, who first started playing the game when she was hardly bigger than a tennis racket.
Peter Graf acted as her mentor, manager and adviser and the two were almost inseparable until he was arrested in August 1995 after tax officials raided their homes.
Prosecutors in March dropped investigations against Steffi Graf herself, who is out of the game at the moment with a knee injury, after she agreed to make a donation to charity.
Media reports put the sum at 1.3 million marks ($700,000). Steffi says she knew little about her financial affairs, entrusting them to her father from the start of her career.

The 28-year-old, who has slipped to fifth place in the world rankings, was unable to defend her Wimbledon title in June and will miss the U.S. Open, has recently said she was considering retiring because of persistent injuries.
